docs.text: Our primary research vessel for the , the CCGS Limnos, left this afternoon for an 8 day research and monitoring mission to support the 🇨🇦🇺🇸 Cooperative Science and Monitoring Initiative field year for . This spring cruise is in collaboration with Environment and Climate Change Canada , and we are collecting chemical, biological, and contaminants samples for many partners, including , , and others.

Time for updated with the new influx of users from dysfunctional Twitter. I'm a Research Scientist working for Fisheries and Oceans () based out of the Canada Centre for Inland Waters in Burlington. My group is responsible for lower trophic (microbes, phytoplankton, and diets of forage ). This supports recreational & commercial fisheries and ecosystem health in the lakes. Sunday

Thus far OLF seems to be going well, (at least from a back of the house standpoint). Got my meshtastic display / presentation setup with a working live node to demonstrate communication and environmental sensor support. A good number of folks asking about the tech, which is always fun! Oh yeah, and the occasional cosplayer in full attire wandering through is good entertainment too.

A very nice day 😎 today for some on the Fisheries and Oceans Canada () R.V. Cisco within Harbour. The team from Buffalo State is out collecting benthos with Ponar sampler and drop-down camera (Benthic Imaging System) to complement our monitoring project looking at zooplankton and phytoplankton in the Harbour, which is impacted by (low or no oxygen) during the summer.

It was an adventure for my staff out sampling off the 🇨🇦 Coast Guard Ship, Samuel Risley icebreaker last week on Lake Huron. Ice everywhere for sampling water properties, chemistry, phytoplankton and zooplankton during the binational . Many lessons learned about the difficulties of ship-based winter , including frozen sensors and some damaged equipment. However, it was a success due to the support of the crew.

The 🇨🇦🇺🇸 cruise is moving along nicely on the CCGS . The stations off Oswego, NY take a little longer because these are the deepwater stations for Lake Ontario with max depth of 244 meters (802 feet). These are stations where we will most likely catch Mysis diluviana, an important . We should be done the US waters stations by end of today and move to the north shore to complete the survey.

The last DFO mission of the year on our research ship Limnos is usually a Mysid cruise. We are sampling fall zooplankton and Mysis diluviana (oppossum shrimp) which is an important prey species in the . In late Oct / early Nov the weather is often poor, and we were blown of the lake for most of this week (crew very ill with rough seas). The crew got two transects in this weekend and even caught some . Night sampling is required for Mysis under red lights.🏮

One day into the DFO-ECCC monitoring cruise and we have completed 16 stations. Notice that this is lake-wide sampling - including US waters because water currents and biota cross borders! The Limnos works 24/7 so we have day and night shifts sampling and processing water samples. The ship is currently at Station 33, one of our major long-term monitoring sites which DFO has sampled back to the 1970s.

A little bit of cut and paste magic, and look at the number of vessels working on right now! I found 5 (likely there are additional smaller ones) from (CCGS Limnos), EPA Lake Guardian, USGS Kaho, MNRF Ontario Explorer and NYDEC Seth Green. All with different focus from water quality, foodwebs, and fisheries science.

What do you value about the waterfront? Niagara, Hamilton and Halton conservation authorities want to know In an effort to better understand the Lake Ontario shoreline, three conservation authorities are teaming up and asking residents what they value about the waterfront.

Kingston leaders call on Ontario to support marine conservation in Great Lakes Kingston councillors are calling on the federal and provincial governments to undertake a feasibility assessment for the creation of a protected marine area in Lake Ontario.

The CCGS is busy and full! There are 14 scientists on board from and plus the Coast Guard crew. It is also *HOT 🔥 with the air temperatures over the ridiculously near 30C in April! The engineer rigged up an extra air duct to keep our incubators we use for algal primary productivity cool, because we need to have the water at lake temperature, which is 4-7C. Limnos is currently sampling the deeper stations off Rochester, NY. 🇨🇦🇺🇸

Always nice to see the crew return safely to the Canada Centre for Inland Waters in Burlington from the monthly sampling done for the 2023 🇨🇦🇺🇸 Collaborative Science and Monitoring Initiative . 6 stations, 140 km! Long day and a little rough on the lake, but our biologists and coop students toughed it out. We collected to study lower and water for chemistry and to measure algae and bacteria growth rates.

I am glad this old shipwreck hasn't been entangled in equipment over the years. This zone of Lake Ontario regularly has active surveys using a variety of equipment, including bottom net trawls. Must luckily be in-between standardized stations.

This week had two long days sampling using our RV Cisco, completing two projects. The first was retrieval of several lost fish telemetry receivers. These listen for implanted with acoustics tags. The crew used a Deep Trekker to attach a line and haul up the devices missing for 2 years. The crew then circled the lake collecting water to measure primary productivity ( growth) to match EPA sampling for the binational fieldyear.

A very exciting day with our much delayed 🇨🇦 research ship 🚢 CCGS Limnos sailing to the Welland Canal for sampling on Lake Erie for the Cooperative Science and Monitoring Initiative fieldyear. The ship has been in drydock since last June, and we are so happy to have her back. Science moorings will be deployed, and my Fisheries and Oceans staff & students will be measuring primary productivity, bacterial growth and across .

To begin our sampling, our research ship Limnos has to transit from Lake to Lake using the Welland Canal. It was an exciting experience for our students. This is a 43 km trip, involving 8 locks, rising 100 m total height, since Niagara Falls is rather un-navigable 😉.

This house on an islet near Electric Island off Point au Baril in Lake Huron's has a Pacific Northwest style totem pole. While paddling past thousands of similar houses I've often wondered how their septic systems work. I rely on a Sawyer Squeeze to filter my drinking water.

The Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) Food-webs and Ecosystems Research crew is out on the CCGS Limnos making its way to Lake Erie from Sarnia. They will be sampling , and along with primary productivity measures for our fall survey in support of the binational Cooperative Science and Monitoring Initiative (CSMI). I'll post cruise updates over the next 10 days.

So, an update from my Food-webs team out on the CCGS Limnos. They have been very busy collecting water and zooplankton across the still very green western basin of Lake Erie (even into October) the past two days, but still had the chance to enjoy some views including passing under the now connected Gordie Howe International Bridge linking Windsor and Detroit, and seeing some amazing sunrises and sunsets. 12 stations down another 16 to go.

Because access to a ship like the Limnos is so valuable, we are again sharing this cruise with Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) technical operations group who are servicing and retrieving moorings and meteorological buoys. These are very important instruments used binationally by Canada and US agencies such as NOAA for forecasting not only weather, but also and algal blooms. Dreissena mussels cover these. Many buoys to collect so deck space gets tight!

Our lab at Fisheries and Oceans Canada was involved in the Feb 2022 binational "Winter Grab" which near simultaneously sampled all of the Laurentian . Many partners across the basin including academics, students and government scientists took part. All of the data collected has now been posted and is available this week to anyone to use. Here is the new data paper in Limnology and Oceanography Letters.

Late season fieldwork on the is very much weather dependent so sometimes that means working on the weekend. Kelly and Dallas were out yesterday sampling late season phyto- & , water properties, and water for productivity measures. Covered 400+ km Sat and will add another 300 km today on our RV Cisco.
